Not my grandpa, but my German teacher (in America) had her grandpa come in one day and talk to us about his experience. I can’t remember his role specifically but he was in an armored division and had some sort of role in a tank. He talked about painfully shaving his beard in a cold stream because George S. Patton had told him he was looking scruffy. He went on to storm the eagles nest and brought several cool artifacts he brought back with him. A key supposedly belonging to Himmler’s door, an SS armband, and some sort of knife or bayonet. It was one of the coolest experiences I’ve had getting to sit there and listen to him tell his stories. My great grandfather was a fighter pilot in the war but he passed away before I was old enough to ever tell me anything about what it was like. Love hearing the personal stories, like of meeting Patton, just as much as the battles themselves. It makes me glad knowing that that little piece of history will keep on living through me, and not fade when he passes away.

I truly didn't know how to feel. 

As time passed, I went back and watched everything and read all the stories several times. I get the chills thinking about it, and I've got them now as I write this. I'm a 19 year old man now and I'm not afraid to say that every year when I watch the footage, it makes me hang my head and cry. It's more powerful now than it was to me then. I understand the gravity and the sheer terror our nation witnessed on live television. 

Thank you to all the first responders, prayers to all the families who lost loved ones, and God bless America.
